# Vendored Markmap fork

These packages come from the Markmap fork:

- Source: <https://github.com/mmospanenko/markmap>
- Branch: `feat/relationship-arrows`, commit `d87e5ae0ad41ba517f737ca577e8320bfe204e58`

The fork adds `@markmap/model`, `@markmap/edit`, and `@markmap/edit-dom`, extends `@markmap/parse` and the `@markmap/core` types with source ranges, scales the overlay field with the map zoom, draws a selection frame, supports zero-width empty labels, sizes, centers, and frames the edit field from its text, reveals newly inserted nodes, reports each valid label draft through `onDraftChange` before the first snapshot, keeps `onChange` for committed edits, and publishes the baseline when a label session is cancelled, lost or switched without a duplicate event. A label snapshot is a pure read: it returns the last saveable draft without emitting or committing, while a note snapshot still commits the open note; notes do not emit `onDraftChange` and stay on the snapshot-driven path. Label previews are drawn at most once per animation frame, and a commit reuses the validated preview result and skips a tree render the view already shows. The fork records a completed label session as one undo entry, counts content nodes separately from a synthetic or title root, promotes a lone top-level heading at H1-H6 to the root even when a non-empty frontmatter `title` exists, uses the title as the fallback root label only when no promotion happens, allows root creation for a synthetic root without a top-level H1 and for a title root without heading children, exposes the root policy and the `createRootHeading` command, caps new branches at H2: a child of an H1 root or heading becomes H2, a child of an H2-H6 heading and a sibling of an H3-H6 heading become list items, while H1 and H2 siblings keep their heading level and existing H3-H6 headings stay editable in place, separates a created H1 from the following body with one blank line, preserves whitespace-only input when it creates that heading, moves a node and its subtree by pointer or keyboard, selects sibling nodes with Cmd/Ctrl-click, a Shift range or a plain click, moves or deletes the selected group as one contiguous atomic command, keeps the moved group selected and restores the selection on undo and redo, pastes a Markdown block as a child with heading levels and list indents re-leveled, pastes a copied promoted root with its intro notes attached only when the prefix is exactly those notes, rejects any other prefix without changing the document, converts a heading subtree to list items under a list item, copies a title or promoted root as a heading with its notes and child blocks, and edits notes in one `markmap-note` fenced block under the node with legacy paragraph migration. Review fixes keep BOM offsets aligned before transformer plugins run, support Setext roots and an empty ATX heading with CRLF, report every draft version so the host save tracker can distinguish a newer draft from an older saved version, and treat a command whose source is unchanged as a no-op with no history entry, no committed change, and no redo loss. It reads trailing `<!-- ^id -->` node identities, parses at most one hidden `<!-- markmap: graph -->` block into typed edges and groups, stores no block for an empty graph, validates identity and graph conventions without changing the tree, and keeps graph references consistent through copy, paste, and delete with injected identity minting. A copied subtree drops references to `root`; a copied whole root keeps the original graph block once. The parse result exposes the top-level HTML block ranges the model uses to find that graph block. It also renders group boundaries in an underlay pass with theme tokens `--mm-group-border` and `--mm-group-fill`, shows group labels above the top boundary, conceals groups when folded, creates groups for selected subtrees and contiguous siblings, selects boundaries on click, deletes boundaries on Delete or Backspace with marker cleanup, and edits group labels in place with an inline overlay. The renderer and editor draw relationship arrows as cubic Bezier curves with directional arrowheads and centered labels, hide edges when either endpoint is folded, and support interactive edge creation via drag from connection handles, edge selection, inline label editing, and edge deletion. The toolbar stays on the published package; the renderer and view are vendored with graph, group boundary, relationship, and theme changes.

The vendored render package adds the soft tree theme, per-node label metrics, tapered root edges, group boundary underlays, and relationship arrows. The renderer, view, toolbar, and built-in themes otherwise start from upstream.

Vendored packages:

- `core`: types with `source` ranges, notes, graph edges, and resolved label styles.
- `parse`: parser that promotes a lone H1-H6 heading, reports title presence and body start, and emits `source.label`, `source.block`, and note ranges.
- `model`: editable document projection with root policy, content node count, note ranges, graph metadata, and validator.
- `edit`: source-preserving commands, including `move`, `moveNodes`, `deleteNodes`, `setNotes`, `createRootHeading`, `createGroup`, `deleteGroup`, `setGroupLabel`, `createEdge`, `deleteEdge`, and `setEdgeLabel`.
- `edit-dom`: selection, sibling group selection, keyboard, pointer move, overlay field, notes panel, group boundary selection, group label editing, connection handle drag, edge selection, edge label editing, draft-change channel, snapshots, and history.
- `render`: the soft theme, per-node label metrics, tapered root edges, group boundary underlays, relationship curves, arrowheads, and labels.
- `view`: interactive Markmap view with dynamic graph state synchronization (`setGraph`).

Migration from the earlier fork drop:

- `commitForSnapshot` is `snapshot`.
- `insertFirst` is `createRootHeading`.
- `buildFromTree` requires a `DocumentMeta` argument.
- Wire `onChange` for committed documents and `onDraftChange` for label drafts.

Only `dist` is copied. Run `pnpm verify` in the fork before copying `dist`. Do not copy a partial build. Then copy `dist` again when the fork changes. The vendored `package.json` stays on workspace packages.

The vendored packages are MIT licensed. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).
